title: Biotech reverse mergers rebound to highest level since 2021 as PIPEs flood market: report
summary: Reverse mergers have returned with a bang. More biotechs have taken the back door to the public markets so far in 2026 than in any full year since 2021, according to J.P. Morgan, with institutional investors backing many of the newly public companies from day one.

title: Advocacy organization launches data dashboard to better assess how clinical trial sites perform
summary: The Society for Clinical Research Sites (SCRS) has launched a data intelligence platform to offer fresh insights into how different locations compare.

title: Lycia aims for $228M IPO to generate data on food allergy rival to Xolair
summary: Lycia Therapeutics is banking on a $227.8 million IPO as the biotech seeks to finance its pipeline of protein degraders for autoimmune, inflammatory and allergic diseases.

title: Rapport's phase 2 bipolar win strikes chord with analysts despite falling short of original ambition
summary: Rapport Therapeutics’ phase 2 bipolar mania study has hit its primary endpoint, furthering the biotech’s efforts to make RAP-219 a multiindication blockbuster. However, the effect size fell short of the level targeted by Rapport and analysts ahead of the readout.

title: Industry at a ‘turning point’ with growth dominated by commercial leaders: EY report
summary: A new report has found that in 2025 through the first half of 2026, innovation increased dealmaking and R&D investment, AI heavily influenced the future of value creation, and that industry growth continued to expand into alternative care settings.

title: Israeli biotech’s inhaled exosome therapy reduces respiratory failure in phase 2 study
summary: Nano24’s inhaled exosome therapy reduced respiratory failure in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), hitting the main goal of a phase 2b study.

title: Pfizer makes ‘business decision’ to end phase 2 trial of autoimmune drug as program’s future uncertain
summary: Pfizer has called time on a phase 2 trial of its CXCR5 antibody in an autoimmune blood disorder, with the company tight-lipped on whether this marks the end of the road for the asset.

title: AstraZeneca taps Oracle to help improve recruitment for clinical trials
summary: AstraZeneca has turned to data giant Oracle as the U.K.-based Big Pharma works on one of the eternal problems of drug development—improving patient recruitment.

title: Ambrose Healthcare inks $181M deal for former Pfizer target AM-Pharma
summary: Ambrose Healthcare has bought AM-Pharma for up to 161 million euros, inking a cut-price deal for a biotech once courted by Pfizer.

title: Investment firm TCGX picks migraine biotech TriGemX to take public via SPAC
summary: Life sciences-focused investment firm TCGX will use a special purpose acquisition company to take migraine-minded TriGemX Bio public.

title: Lilly partners with Hong Kong's Metis in $1.1B deal to bolster AI nanoparticle discovery
summary: The collaboration is another in a series of partnerships Lilly has accumulated in both drug delivery and AI-based technologies.

title: Gilead ‘sitting on a foundational asset’ after oral UC drug's phase 2 win
summary: Gilead touted a mid-stage win for its inflammatory bowel disease pill after the treatment delivered clinical improvements in patients with ulcerative colitis.

title: Enlivex lays off 60% of employees, scraps preclinical R&D and gives execs ‘substantial’ salary cuts
summary: Enlivex is laying off 60% of its workforce, ending preclinical R&D and trimming its top execs’ salaries as the Israeli biotech tries to keep cash flowing to its osteoarthritis drug.

title: Merck KGaA buys Silence in $1.3B deal after siRNA drug's phase 2 blood cancer win
summary: Germany’s Merck KGaA has picked up Silence Therapeutics to the tune of $1.3 billion in the wake of the British biotech’s mid-stage success for its challenger to Takeda’s Mimrylo.

title: Disc spins past FDA rejection with ‘overwhelmingly positive’ phase 3 data for rare disease drug
summary: A phase 3 trial of Disc Medicine’s bitopertin has hit both co-primary endpoints and all secondary endpoints, positioning the biotech to refile for approval of the once-rejected rare disease drug candidate.

title: Aligning drug discovery around patient benefit from the outset: Connecting human insights to better decisions
summary: The pharmaceutical industry has traditionally viewed drug discovery and clinical development as separate stages of the R&D continuum.

title: Immune Boost Capital Invests in Orthrus Therapeutics to Advance Antigen-Specific Immune Tolerance for Autoimmune Disease
summary: Immune Boost Capital (IBC), the venture investment arm of the Arthritis National Research Foundation (ANRF), today announced its investment in Orthrus Therapeutics, a company developing a new class of precision therapies for autoimmune disease with a strong focus on rheumatoid arthritis.

title: Siemens Healthineers partners with Paradromics to build out new imaging system to support BCIs
summary: Paradromics has announced a new collaboration with Siemens Healthineers to construct an advanced multimodal imaging platform to support the growing clinical use of implantable brain-computer interfaces (BCIs).

title: Roche returns to China’s ADC powerhouse Hansoh for $15B biobucks pact
summary: A year after their first antibody-drug conjugate team-up, Roche has returned to Hansoh Pharmaceutical for a mammoth $15 billion biobucks pact.

title: AbbVie’s next-gen Crohn’s disease combo beats Skyrizi in phase 2 trial
summary: AbbVie’s next-generation Crohn’s disease combination candidate has beaten Skyrizi in a midphase clinical trial.

title: Nouscom raises $135M for pivotal trial of cancer-preventing vaccine candidate
summary: Nouscom has reeled in 120 million euros ($135 million) to take a cancer-preventing vaccine through a registration-enabling clinical trial.

A corticohypothalamic circuit that mediates maternal awakening to pup cries
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02458-yTang, Wu et al. identify a brain circuit that enables mother mice to wake selectively to pup cries. Motherhood strengthens this pathway through increased dopamine receptor D1 expression, helping mothers to be responsive to offspring during sleep.

title: SIK3 controls synaptic localization of NMDA receptors by phosphorylating GluN1
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02469-9SIK3 kinase controls synaptic NMDA receptor recruitment by phosphorylating GluN1 at a single site. Loss or inhibition of SIK3 markedly reduces synaptic NMDARs, while a gain-of-function mutation increases GluN1 phosphorylation and NMDAR levels.

title: Dysregulated cholesterol trafficking through ABCA1 drives neurodegeneration in Parkinson’s disease
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02487-7This study identifies ABCA1 as a driver of dysregulated cholesterol trafficking in Parkinson’s disease, showing that reducing ABCA1 in astrocytes and neurons decreases cholesterol accumulation, α-synuclein pathology and neurodegeneration in mice.

title: Spatiotemporal remodeling in habenula marks the onset of depression-related phenotypes
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02488-6Molina et al. show in chronically stressed mice that neuronal and transcriptional adaptations in the habenula coincide with the onset of depressive phenotype, guiding temporally defined antidepressant interventions.

title: An amygdala-mediated simulation-to-decision cascade aligns interbrain dynamics to solve social dilemmas
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02473-zUsing simultaneous intracranial recordings from interacting human brains, Ma et al. show that mutual cooperation emerges when amygdala activity aligns across partners and predictions about a partner guide each person’s own decisions.

title: 5-HT2A receptors in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediate the neuroplastic but not the hallucinogenic effects of psilocybin
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02490-yPsilocybin promotes and stabilizes new connections between neurons in the mouse cerebral cortex, especially after stress. Baker et al. show that 5-HT2A receptor signaling in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediates this effect but is not required for a mouse behavioral proxy of hallucinations.

title: A half-center oscillator regulates sleep pressure
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02431-9Hasenhuetl et al. show that neurons innervating the dorsal fan-shaped body of Drosophila form a half-center oscillator, a circuit motif typically found in central pattern generators for locomotion. Here, this circuit generates slow-wave activity for the regulation of sleep.

title: Why AI Cannot Replace the Transformative Power of Human Creativity
summary: Generative AI can create masterpieces in seconds, but a new analysis reveals it breaks the crucial link between making art and personal growth. Hebrew University's Amit Zoran argues that the future of creativity belongs to human discovery and perspective rather than automated digital output.
